# pipenv
#   According to pypa/pipenv#598, it is recommended to include Pipfile.lock in version control.
#   However, in case of collaboration, if having platform-specific dependencies or dependencies
#   having no cross-platform support, pipenv may install dependencies that don't work, or not
#   install all needed dependencies.

# poetry
#   Similar to Pipfile.lock, it is generally recommended to include poetry.lock in version control.
#   This is especially recommended for binary packages to ensure reproducibility, and is more
#   commonly ignored for libraries.
#   https://python-poetry.org/docs/basic-usage/#commit-your-poetrylock-file-to-version-control

--- FILE: elec/README.md ---
# my_first_ato_project

A brand new atopile project!

Created by Pepper Powderly <pepper@atopile.io>

--- FILE: elec/adc.ato ---
"""
ADC front-end: 2x ADS1115 + input protection + excitation filter.

Signal path per thermistor channel:
  J2 pin → [TVS ESD pin] → R_AIN (1k) → [C_AIN 100nF to GND] → ADC AIN pin

Excitation path:
  MCU GPIO → R_EXC (560 ohm) → filtered_exc → C_EXC (1uF to GND)
                                      |→ J2 pin 4 (excitation to sensor)
                                      |→ R_AIN_EXC (1k) → [TVS + C_AIN_EXC] → ADC1 AIN3

TVS arrays (PRTR5V0U4D):
  D_J2A: excitation sense + thermistors 1-3 (4 channels)
  D_J2B: thermistors 4-6 + unused ESD4 (tied to GND)

ADC1 (0x48): AIN0-AIN2 = thermistors 1-3, AIN3 = excitation sense
ADC2 (0x49): AIN0-AIN2 = thermistors 4-6, AIN3 = unused
"""

#pragma experiment("BRIDGE_CONNECT")

import Resistor
import ElectricPower
import Electrical

from "atopile/ti-ads1115/ti-ads1115.ato" import TI_ADS1115
from "parts/TECH_PUBLIC_PRTR5V0U4D_TP/TECH_PUBLIC_PRTR5V0U4D_TP.ato" import TECH_PUBLIC_PRTR5V0U4D_TP_package
from "parts/YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104/YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104.ato" import YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
from "parts/Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC/Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC.ato" import Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC_package

module ADCFrontEnd:
    """
    2x ADS1115 16-bit ADCs with 7-channel input protection (RC filters + TVS)
    and excitation filter for thermistor measurement.
    """

    # --- External interfaces ---
    power = new ElectricPower
    """3.3V supply for ADCs and TVS arrays."""

    sda = new Electrical
    """I2C SDA line (shared bus, wired in top-level)."""

    scl = new Electrical
    """I2C SCL line (shared bus, wired in top-level)."""

    excitation_gpio = new Electrical
    """MCU GPIO output driving thermistor excitation."""

    excitation_out = new Electrical
    """Filtered excitation to J2 connector (sensor cable)."""

    thermistor_1 = new Electrical
    thermistor_2 = new Electrical
    thermistor_3 = new Electrical
    thermistor_4 = new Electrical
    thermistor_5 = new Electrical
    thermistor_6 = new Electrical

    alert1 = new Electrical
    """ADC1 ALERT/DRDY output to MCU."""

    alert2 = new Electrical
    """ADC2 ALERT/DRDY output to MCU."""

    # --- ADC instances (registry package includes decoupling + I2C pull-ups + ALERT pull-up) ---
    adc1 = new TI_ADS1115
    adc2 = new TI_ADS1115

    # Power
    power ~ adc1.power
    power ~ adc2.power

    # I2C (direct line connections, avoid interface-level merging issues)
    sda ~ adc1.i2c.sda.line
    sda ~ adc2.i2c.sda.line
    scl ~ adc1.i2c.scl.line
    scl ~ adc2.i2c.scl.line

    # Addresses: ADC1 = 0x48 (default), ADC2 = 0x49
    # Addressor handles ADDR pin wiring internally
    adc2.addressor.address = 0x49

    # Tie unused ADC2 AIN3 to GND (prevents floating input from coupling noise)
    adc2.inputs[3].line ~ power.lv

    # ALERT/DRDY
    alert1 ~ adc1.alert_ready.line
    alert2 ~ adc2.alert_ready.line

    # --- Excitation filter (R_EXC + C_EXC) ---
    r_exc = new Resistor
    r_exc.resistance = 560ohm +/- 1%
    r_exc.package = "0603"

    c_exc = new Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC_package
    """1uF 50V. RC = 560 ohm x 1uF = 560us, fc = 284Hz."""

    filtered_exc = new Electrical

    excitation_gpio ~> r_exc ~> filtered_exc
    filtered_exc ~ c_exc.p1
    c_exc.p2 ~ power.lv
    filtered_exc ~ excitation_out

    # --- TVS arrays ---
    d_j2a = new TECH_PUBLIC_PRTR5V0U4D_TP_package
    d_j2b = new TECH_PUBLIC_PRTR5V0U4D_TP_package

    d_j2a.VCC ~ power.hv
    d_j2a.GND ~ power.lv
    d_j2b.VCC ~ power.hv
    d_j2b.GND ~ power.lv
    d_j2b.ESD4 ~ power.lv

    # Local decoupling for TVS arrays (absorbs ESD dump current, prevents 3.3V rail bounce)
    c_esd_a = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
    c_esd_b = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
    c_esd_a.p1 ~ power.hv
    c_esd_a.p2 ~ power.lv
    c_esd_b.p1 ~ power.hv
    c_esd_b.p2 ~ power.lv

    # --- Input protection: 7 channels (1k series R + 100nF shunt C each) ---

    # Series resistors (auto-pick 1k 0603)
    r_ain1 = new Resistor
    r_ain1.resistance = 1kohm +/- 1%
    r_ain1.package = "0603"
    r_ain2 = new Resistor
    r_ain2.resistance = 1kohm +/- 1%
    r_ain2.package = "0603"
    r_ain3 = new Resistor
    r_ain3.resistance = 1kohm +/- 1%
    r_ain3.package = "0603"
    r_ain4 = new Resistor
    r_ain4.resistance = 1kohm +/- 1%
    r_ain4.package = "0603"
    r_ain5 = new Resistor
    r_ain5.resistance = 1kohm +/- 1%
    r_ain5.package = "0603"
    r_ain6 = new Resistor
    r_ain6.resistance = 1kohm +/- 1%
    r_ain6.package = "0603"
    r_ain_exc = new Resistor
    r_ain_exc.resistance = 1kohm +/- 1%
    r_ain_exc.package = "0603"

    # Filter caps (100nF 50V explicit for voltage rating)
    c_ain1 = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
    c_ain2 = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
    c_ain3 = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
    c_ain4 = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
    c_ain5 = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
    c_ain6 = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
    c_ain_exc = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package

    # Protected nodes (after series R, at TVS/cap/ADC junction)
    prot_1 = new Electrical
    prot_2 = new Electrical
    prot_3 = new Electrical
    prot_4 = new Electrical
    prot_5 = new Electrical
    prot_6 = new Electrical
    prot_exc = new Electrical

    # === Ch1: thermistor_1 → ADC1 AIN0, TVS D_J2A.ESD2 ===
    thermistor_1 ~ d_j2a.ESD2
    thermistor_1 ~> r_ain1 ~> prot_1
    prot_1 ~ c_ain1.p1
    c_ain1.p2 ~ power.lv
    prot_1 ~ adc1.inputs[0].line

    # === Ch2: thermistor_2 → ADC1 AIN1, TVS D_J2A.ESD3 ===
    thermistor_2 ~ d_j2a.ESD3
    thermistor_2 ~> r_ain2 ~> prot_2
    prot_2 ~ c_ain2.p1
    c_ain2.p2 ~ power.lv
    prot_2 ~ adc1.inputs[1].line

    # === Ch3: thermistor_3 → ADC1 AIN2, TVS D_J2A.ESD4 ===
    thermistor_3 ~ d_j2a.ESD4
    thermistor_3 ~> r_ain3 ~> prot_3
    prot_3 ~ c_ain3.p1
    c_ain3.p2 ~ power.lv
    prot_3 ~ adc1.inputs[2].line

    # === Ch4: thermistor_4 → ADC2 AIN0, TVS D_J2B.ESD1 ===
    thermistor_4 ~ d_j2b.ESD1
    thermistor_4 ~> r_ain4 ~> prot_4
    prot_4 ~ c_ain4.p1
    c_ain4.p2 ~ power.lv
    prot_4 ~ adc2.inputs[0].line

    # === Ch5: thermistor_5 → ADC2 AIN1, TVS D_J2B.ESD2 ===
    thermistor_5 ~ d_j2b.ESD2
    thermistor_5 ~> r_ain5 ~> prot_5
    prot_5 ~ c_ain5.p1
    c_ain5.p2 ~ power.lv
    prot_5 ~ adc2.inputs[1].line

    # === Ch6: thermistor_6 → ADC2 AIN2, TVS D_J2B.ESD3 ===
    thermistor_6 ~ d_j2b.ESD3
    thermistor_6 ~> r_ain6 ~> prot_6
    prot_6 ~ c_ain6.p1
    c_ain6.p2 ~ power.lv
    prot_6 ~ adc2.inputs[2].line

    # === Excitation sense → ADC1 AIN3, TVS D_J2A.ESD1 ===
    filtered_exc ~ d_j2a.ESD1
    filtered_exc ~> r_ain_exc ~> prot_exc
    prot_exc ~ c_ain_exc.p1
    c_ain_exc.p2 ~ power.lv
    prot_exc ~ adc1.inputs[3].line

--- FILE: elec/buck.ato ---
"""
LM5165Y buck converter: 24V protected input to 3.3V output.

PFM mode (RT shorted to GND) for 10.5uA quiescent current.
RILIM = 56k for 120mA peak / 50mA max PFM output.
Design follows TI Design 2 (Section 8.2.2, Figure 50).

Topology:
  VIN (24V) --+-- C1 (4.7uF 50V) --+-- GND
              |                      |
              +-- C_VIN (100nF 50V) -+
              |
           U_BUCK.VIN
              |
           U_BUCK.SW --- L1 (68uH) --- VOUT (3.3V)
              |                           |
           U_BUCK.VOUT --+-- C2 (22uF) --+-- GND
                         |
                         +-- C6 (1uF 50V) --- GND

  RT -> GND (PFM mode)
  EN -> VIN (always on, internal UVLO at 2.9V)
  ILIM -> R_ILIM (56k) -> GND
  SS -> open, HYS -> open
  EP -> GND
  PGOOD -> MCU (open-drain, needs external pull-up)

Note: LM5165 VSON-10 has internal bootstrap — no external BST cap needed.
"""

#pragma experiment("BRIDGE_CONNECT")

import Resistor
import ElectricPower
import ElectricLogic

from "parts/Texas_Instruments_LM5165YDRCR/Texas_Instruments_LM5165YDRCR.ato" import Texas_Instruments_LM5165YDRCR_package
from "parts/XR_XRNR4018_68uH_M/XR_XRNR4018_68uH_M.ato" import XR_XRNR4018_68uH_M_package
from "parts/FH_1206B475K500NT/FH_1206B475K500NT.ato" import FH_1206B475K500NT_package
from "parts/TDK_C2012X5R1A226KT000N/TDK_C2012X5R1A226KT000N.ato" import TDK_C2012X5R1A226KT000N_package
from "parts/YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104/YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104.ato" import YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
from "parts/Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC/Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC.ato" import Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC_package

module BuckConverter:
    """
    LM5165Y synchronous buck: 24V -> 3.3V, PFM mode, 10.5uA Iq.
    150mA max output, 120mA peak current limit (RILIM=56k).
    """

    # --- External interfaces ---
    power_in = new ElectricPower
    """24V protected input rail."""

    power_out = new ElectricPower
    """3.3V regulated output rail."""

    pgood = new ElectricLogic
    """
    Power-good output (open-drain). Goes high when 3.3V is in regulation.
    Needs external 10k pull-up to 3.3V (in MCU module).
    """

    # --- IC ---
    u_buck = new Texas_Instruments_LM5165YDRCR_package

    # --- Inductor ---
    l1 = new XR_XRNR4018_68uH_M_package
    """68uH, 470mA Isat, 1 ohm DCR, 4x4mm shielded."""

    # --- Input capacitors (24V rail, need 50V rating) ---
    c1 = new FH_1206B475K500NT_package
    """4.7uF 50V X7R, 1206. Bulk input energy reservoir."""

    c_vin = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
    """100nF 50V, 0603. HF decoupling tight to VIN/GND pins."""

    # --- Output capacitors ---
    c2 = new TDK_C2012X5R1A226KT000N_package
    """22uF 10V X5R, 0805. Output ripple smoothing."""

    c6 = new Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC_package
    """1uF 50V X5R, 0603. Internal VCC LDO decoupling on VOUT."""

    # --- Current limit resistor ---
    r_ilim = new Resistor
    r_ilim.resistance = 56kohm +/- 1%
    r_ilim.package = "0603"

    # === Power connections ===

    # VIN rail
    power_in.hv ~ u_buck.VIN
    power_in.hv ~ c1.p1
    power_in.hv ~ c_vin.p1

    # Input caps to GND
    c1.p2 ~ power_in.lv
    c_vin.p2 ~ power_in.lv

    # GND connections
    power_in.lv ~ u_buck.GND
    power_in.lv ~ u_buck.EP
    power_in.lv ~ power_out.lv

    # === Control pin connections ===

    # EN -> VIN (always on; internal UVLO at 2.9V handles startup)
    u_buck.EN ~ power_in.hv

    # RT -> GND (PFM mode, no timing resistor)
    u_buck.RT ~ power_in.lv

    # ILIM -> 56k -> GND (120mA peak current limit)
    u_buck.ILIM ~> r_ilim ~> power_in.lv

    # SS -> open (internal 900us soft-start) — no connection needed
    # HYS -> open — no connection needed

    # === Output path ===

    # SW -> L1 -> VOUT
    u_buck.SW ~ l1.p1
    l1.p2 ~ u_buck.VOUT

    # VOUT rail
    u_buck.VOUT ~ power_out.hv
    u_buck.VOUT ~ c2.p1
    u_buck.VOUT ~ c6.p1

    # Output caps to GND
    c2.p2 ~ power_out.lv
    c6.p2 ~ power_out.lv

    # === PGOOD output ===
    u_buck.PGOOD ~ pgood.line
    pgood.reference ~ power_out

--- FILE: elec/connectors.ato ---
"""
Connectors: M8 upstream (J1) + 10-pin sensor header (J2) + shield cap.

J1 (M8 4-pin A-coded):
  Pin 1: 24V power input
  Pin 2: RS-485 A (+)
  Pin 3: GND
  Pin 4: RS-485 B (-)
  Shell: C5 (100nF) to GND

J2 (KF2EDGV 10-pin 3.5mm):
  Pin 1-2: Heater A/B (24V, non-polar)
  Pin 3: Ground
  Pin 4: Excitation (filtered 3.3V)
  Pin 5-10: Data 1-6 (thermistors)
"""

import ElectricPower
import Electrical

from "parts/CAZN_M8_P4A_GPL_M8_JD/CAZN_M8_P4A_GPL_M8_JD.ato" import CAZN_M8_P4A_GPL_M8_JD_package
from "parts/Cixi_Kefa_Elec_KF2EDGV_3_5_10P/Cixi_Kefa_Elec_KF2EDGV_3_5_10P.ato" import Cixi_Kefa_Elec_KF2EDGV_3_5_10P_package
from "parts/YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104/YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104.ato" import YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package

module Connectors:
    """M8 upstream connector, 10-pin sensor header, and shield cap."""

    # --- External interfaces ---
    power_24v = new ElectricPower
    """24V raw power from M8 connector."""

    rs485_a = new Electrical
    """RS-485 A line."""

    rs485_b = new Electrical
    """RS-485 B line."""

    heater_hi = new Electrical
    """Heater positive terminal."""

    heater_lo = new Electrical
    """Heater negative terminal."""

    excitation = new Electrical
    """Filtered excitation output to sensor."""

    thermistor_1 = new Electrical
    thermistor_2 = new Electrical
    thermistor_3 = new Electrical
    thermistor_4 = new Electrical
    thermistor_5 = new Electrical
    thermistor_6 = new Electrical

    # --- J1: M8 upstream connector ---
    j1 = new CAZN_M8_P4A_GPL_M8_JD_package

    j1.V24 ~ power_24v.hv
    j1.GND ~ power_24v.lv
    j1.RS485_A ~ rs485_a
    j1.RS485_B ~ rs485_b

    # Shield cap (100nF, blocks ground loop DC, passes HF EMI)
    signal M8_SHIELD ~ j1.SHELL1
    c5 = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
    M8_SHIELD ~ c5.p1
    c5.p2 ~ power_24v.lv
    j1.SHELL2 ~ M8_SHIELD

    # --- J2: 10-pin sensor header ---
    j2 = new Cixi_Kefa_Elec_KF2EDGV_3_5_10P_package

    j2.HEATER_A ~ heater_hi
    j2.HEATER_B ~ heater_lo
    j2.GND ~ power_24v.lv
    j2.EXCITATION ~ excitation
    j2.DATA1 ~ thermistor_1
    j2.DATA2 ~ thermistor_2
    j2.DATA3 ~ thermistor_3
    j2.DATA4 ~ thermistor_4
    j2.DATA5 ~ thermistor_5
    j2.DATA6 ~ thermistor_6

--- FILE: elec/heater.ato ---
"""
Heater driver + TPL5010 watchdog + SCR latch safety circuit.

Q1 (XCHS3N12 N-FET) switches 24V heater current. TPL5010 external watchdog
provides MCU-independent kill via PNP/NPN SCR latch. D_ISO isolates latch
from NRST so MCU can still boot and report fault.

PGOOD-gated arming: Q_ARM (N-FET in R_FB path) prevents the latch from
self-sustaining until RC-delayed PGOOD charges arm_node above Vgs(th).
This prevents the TPL5010 power-on reset (~60ms) from permanently
triggering the latch at every boot. Arming delay ≥361ms (3.6× margin).

Gate-kill circuit:
  MCU timer → R_GATE (1k) → gate_node → R4 (10k) → GND
                                  ↑
                             Q_WD drain
                             Q_WD source → GND
                             Q_WD gate ← Q2_INV collector → R_FB (100k) → Q_ARM → Q_LATCH base
                                            ↑                               ↑          ↑
                                      R_WD_PD (10k) → GND           arm_node    R_LATCH_PD (1M) → GND
                                      Q2_INV emitter → 3.3V            ↑        Q_LATCH emitter → GND
                                      Q2_INV base ← R_BASE (10k) ← D_ISO ← RSTn
                                            ↑  ↑          (anode)   (cathode)    ↑
                                            |  R_PNP_BASE (100k) → 3.3V
                                      Q_LATCH collector          R_WD_PU (100k) → 3.3V

Latch arm circuit:
  PGOOD → R_ARM (1M) → arm_node → C_ARM (1uF) → GND
                           ↑
                      Q_ARM gate
"""

#pragma experiment("BRIDGE_CONNECT")

import Resistor
import ElectricPower
import Electrical

from "parts/XCH_XCHS3N12/XCH_XCHS3N12.ato" import XCH_XCHS3N12_package
from "parts/MDD_Microdiode_Electronics_SS36/MDD_Microdiode_Electronics_SS36.ato" import MDD_Microdiode_Electronics_SS36_package
from "parts/Texas_Instruments_TPL5010DDCR/Texas_Instruments_TPL5010DDCR.ato" import Texas_Instruments_TPL5010DDCR_package
from "parts/Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_SS8550_Y2_RANGE_200_350/Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_SS8550_Y2_RANGE_200_350.ato" import Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_SS8550_Y2_RANGE_200_350_package
from "parts/Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_2N7002/Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_2N7002.ato" import Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_2N7002_package
from "parts/Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_1N4148WS/Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_1N4148WS.ato" import Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_1N4148WS_package
from "parts/Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_MMBT3904_RANGE_100_300/Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_MMBT3904_RANGE_100_300.ato" import Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_MMBT3904_RANGE_100_300_package
from "parts/Honor_Elec_VP1H101M0607/Honor_Elec_VP1H101M0607.ato" import Honor_Elec_VP1H101M0607_package
from "parts/YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104/YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104.ato" import YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
from "parts/Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC/Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC.ato" import Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC_package

module HeaterDriver:
    """
    24V heater driver with 4-layer safety: hardware timer, IWDG, external
    watchdog (TPL5010), and thermistor interlock. SCR latch provides
    permanent lockout on watchdog fault.
    """

    # --- External interfaces ---
    power_24v = new ElectricPower
    """24V protected rail (heater power + bulk cap)."""

    power_3v3 = new ElectricPower
    """3.3V rail (watchdog, PNP emitter, pull-ups)."""

    heater_hi = new Electrical
    """Heater positive terminal (from J2, connects to 24V)."""

    heater_lo = new Electrical
    """Heater negative terminal (from J2, connects to Q1 drain)."""

    gate_drive = new Electrical
    """MCU timer output (into R_GATE)."""

    wake = new Electrical
    """TPL5010 WAKE output → MCU EXTI input."""

    done = new Electrical
    """TPL5010 DONE input ← MCU GPIO output."""

    rstn = new Electrical
    """TPL5010 RSTn node. Also connects to MCU NRST (wired in top-level)."""

    pgood = new Electrical
    """PGOOD signal from buck converter. Gates latch arming via RC delay."""

    # --- Power FET and flyback ---
    q1 = new XCH_XCHS3N12_package
    """120V/3A N-FET heater switch."""

    d4 = new MDD_Microdiode_Electronics_SS36_package
    """60V/3A flyback Schottky across heater."""

    # --- Bulk decoupling on 24V ---
    c4 = new Honor_Elec_VP1H101M0607_package
    """100uF 50V electrolytic. Absorbs heater switching transients."""

    # --- TPL5010 watchdog ---
    u_wdt = new Texas_Instruments_TPL5010DDCR_package

    c_wd = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
    """100nF bypass on TPL5010 VDD."""

    r_delay = new Resistor
    r_delay.resistance = 11kohm +/- 1%
    r_delay.package = "0603"

    # --- Gate control resistors ---
    r_gate = new Resistor
    r_gate.resistance = 1kohm +/- 1%
    r_gate.package = "0603"

    r4 = new Resistor
    r4.resistance = 10kohm +/- 1%
    r4.package = "0603"

    # --- SCR latch components ---
    q2_inv = new Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_SS8550_Y2_RANGE_200_350_package
    """PNP inverter. Inverts RSTn to drive gate clamp."""

    q_wd = new Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_2N7002_package
    """N-FET gate clamp. Pulls Q1 gate to GND on fault."""

    q_latch = new Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_MMBT3904_RANGE_100_300_package
    """NPN latch. Cross-coupled with Q2_INV for permanent lockout."""

    d_iso = new Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_1N4148WS_package
    """Isolation diode. Prevents latch from holding MCU in reset."""

    r_base = new Resistor
    r_base.resistance = 10kohm +/- 1%
    r_base.package = "0603"

    r_wd_pd = new Resistor
    r_wd_pd.resistance = 10kohm +/- 1%
    r_wd_pd.package = "0603"

    r_wd_pu = new Resistor
    r_wd_pu.resistance = 100kohm +/- 1%
    r_wd_pu.package = "0603"

    r_fb = new Resistor
    r_fb.resistance = 100kohm +/- 1%
    r_fb.package = "0603"

    r_latch_pd = new Resistor
    r_latch_pd.resistance = 1Mohm +/- 1%
    r_latch_pd.package = "0603"

    r_pnp_base = new Resistor
    r_pnp_base.resistance = 100kohm +/- 1%
    r_pnp_base.package = "0603"
    """PNP base-emitter pull-up. Defines OFF state when D_ISO is reverse-biased
    and Q_LATCH is off (normal operation). Without this, the PNP base floats
    and leakage/noise could cause spurious heater lockout. 100kΩ gives 140×
    margin over worst-case transistor leakage at 85°C, while still allowing
    easy latch trigger (hFE needed = 1.4 vs MMBT3904 min 100)."""

    # --- PGOOD-gated latch arm circuit ---
    q_arm = new Changjiang_Electronics_Tech_2N7002_package
    """N-FET in R_FB path. Breaks latch feedback loop until PGOOD charges
    arm_node above Vgs(th). Prevents TPL5010 power-on reset from triggering
    permanent heater lockout."""

    r_arm = new Resistor
    r_arm.resistance = 1Mohm +/- 1%
    r_arm.package = "0603"
    """Slow-charge resistor for arm RC delay. τ = 1MΩ × 1µF = 1s.
    Arming delay ≥361ms (Vgs(th) min) vs 100ms max TPL5010 tRST."""

    c_arm = new Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC_package
    """1µF arm delay cap. Holds arm_node low during power-on reset,
    preventing latch feedback until RC charges past Q_ARM threshold."""

    # --- Internal nodes ---
    gate_node = new Electrical
    """Q1 gate: R_GATE output, R4 top, Q_WD drain."""

    pnp_coll_node = new Electrical
    """Q2_INV collector: R_WD_PD top, Q_WD gate, R_FB input."""

    pnp_base_node = new Electrical
    """Q2_INV base: R_BASE output, Q_LATCH collector."""

    d_iso_anode_node = new Electrical
    """D_ISO anode: R_BASE input (between D_ISO and PNP base)."""

    fb_out_node = new Electrical
    """R_FB output / Q_ARM drain junction."""

    latch_base_node = new Electrical
    """Q_LATCH base: Q_ARM source, R_LATCH_PD top."""

    arm_node = new Electrical
    """PGOOD-delayed arm signal. RC charges from PGOOD through R_ARM."""

    # === Heater power path ===

    # 24V → heater_hi, heater_lo → Q1 → GND
    heater_hi ~ power_24v.hv
    heater_lo ~ q1.D
    q1.S ~ power_24v.lv

    # Flyback diode across heater (anode at Q1 drain, cathode at 24V)
    d4.A ~ heater_lo
    d4.K ~ heater_hi

    # Bulk cap on 24V rail
    power_24v.hv ~ c4.p1
    c4.p2 ~ power_24v.lv

    # === Gate drive path ===

    # MCU timer → R_GATE → gate_node → R4 → GND
    gate_drive ~> r_gate ~> gate_node
    gate_node ~> r4 ~> power_24v.lv

    # Q1 gate
    gate_node ~ q1.G

    # Q_WD clamps gate to GND on fault
    q_wd.D ~ gate_node
    q_wd.S ~ power_24v.lv

    # === TPL5010 watchdog ===

    u_wdt.VDD ~ power_3v3.hv
    u_wdt.GND ~ power_3v3.lv

    # Bypass cap
    power_3v3.hv ~ c_wd.p1
    c_wd.p2 ~ power_3v3.lv

    # Timeout resistor (11k → ~9.6s period)
    u_wdt.DELAY_M_RST ~> r_delay ~> power_3v3.lv

    # MCU interface
    u_wdt.WAKE ~ wake
    u_wdt.DONE ~ done

    # DONE pull-down: keeps DONE low when MCU is in reset/unpowered,
    # preventing floating input from confusing TPL5010
    r_done_pd = new Resistor
    r_done_pd.resistance = 100kohm +/- 1%
    r_done_pd.package = "0603"
    done ~> r_done_pd ~> power_3v3.lv

    # RSTn with pull-up
    u_wdt.RSTn ~ rstn
    rstn ~> r_wd_pu ~> power_3v3.hv

    # === SCR latch circuit ===

    # PNP inverter (Q2_INV): emitter → 3.3V, base via R_BASE/D_ISO
    q2_inv.E ~ power_3v3.hv
    q2_inv.B ~ pnp_base_node
    q2_inv.C ~ pnp_coll_node

    # PNP collector drives Q_WD gate + feedback (through PGOOD-gated Q_ARM)
    pnp_coll_node ~ q_wd.G
    pnp_coll_node ~> r_wd_pd ~> power_3v3.lv
    pnp_coll_node ~> r_fb ~> fb_out_node

    # Q_ARM gates the feedback path: latch can't sustain until armed
    q_arm.D ~ fb_out_node
    q_arm.S ~ latch_base_node
    q_arm.G ~ arm_node

    # D_ISO: cathode at RSTn, anode → R_BASE → PNP base
    d_iso.K ~ rstn
    d_iso.A ~ d_iso_anode_node
    d_iso_anode_node ~> r_base ~> pnp_base_node

    # NPN latch (Q_LATCH): collector → PNP base node, emitter → GND
    q_latch.C ~ pnp_base_node
    q_latch.E ~ power_3v3.lv
    q_latch.B ~ latch_base_node

    # PNP base-emitter pull-up (defines OFF state in normal operation)
    pnp_base_node ~> r_pnp_base ~> power_3v3.hv

    # === PGOOD-gated latch arm ===

    # RC delay: PGOOD → R_ARM (1MΩ) → arm_node → C_ARM (1µF) → GND
    # τ = 1s. Arming delay ≥361ms (worst-case Vgs(th)=1.0V) vs 100ms max tRST.
    # At power-on: arm_node low → Q_ARM off → R_FB disconnected → latch disabled.
    # After ~400-800ms: arm_node charged → Q_ARM on → latch armed for real faults.
    pgood ~> r_arm ~> arm_node
    arm_node ~ c_arm.p1
    c_arm.p2 ~ power_3v3.lv

    # Latch base pull-down (noise immunity)
    latch_base_node ~> r_latch_pd ~> power_3v3.lv

--- FILE: elec/led.ato ---
"""
Status RGB LED: common-anode, MCU sinks current through resistors.

  3.3V → LED anode
  LED R cathode → R_R (680 ohm) → MCU GPIO (sink)
  LED G cathode → R_G (200 ohm) → MCU GPIO (sink)
  LED B cathode → R_B (220 ohm) → MCU GPIO (sink)
"""

#pragma experiment("BRIDGE_CONNECT")

import Resistor
import ElectricPower
import Electrical

from "parts/XINGLIGHT_XL_B1212RGBA_HF/XINGLIGHT_XL_B1212RGBA_HF.ato" import XINGLIGHT_XL_B1212RGBA_HF_package

module StatusLED:
    """Common-anode RGB LED with current-limiting resistors."""

    # --- External interfaces ---
    power = new ElectricPower
    """3.3V supply (anode connection)."""

    red = new Electrical
    """MCU GPIO sink for red LED."""

    green = new Electrical
    """MCU GPIO sink for green LED."""

    blue = new Electrical
    """MCU GPIO sink for blue LED."""

    # --- LED ---
    led = new XINGLIGHT_XL_B1212RGBA_HF_package

    # --- Current-limiting resistors ---
    r_r = new Resistor
    r_r.resistance = 680ohm +/- 1%
    r_r.package = "0603"

    r_g = new Resistor
    r_g.resistance = 200ohm +/- 1%
    r_g.package = "0603"

    r_b = new Resistor
    r_b.resistance = 220ohm +/- 1%
    r_b.package = "0603"

    # --- Wiring ---
    # Anode to 3.3V
    led.A ~ power.hv

    # Cathodes through resistors to MCU GPIOs
    led.R ~> r_r ~> red
    led.G ~> r_g ~> green
    led.B ~> r_b ~> blue

--- FILE: elec/main.ato ---
"""
Sap Flux Sensor Adapter Board — atopile implementation.
24V battery/solar powered, RS-485 comms, STM32G0B1 MCU,
2x ADS1115 ADCs, heater driver with TPL5010 watchdog.

Top-level wiring: connects all subsystem modules, assigns MCU GPIOs,
wires connectors, and establishes shared buses (I2C, power rails).

MCU GPIO assignment (STM32G0B1CBT6 LQFP-48):
  PA0: RS-485 ~RE         PA8: TIM1_CH1 (heater gate)
  PA1: RS-485 DE          PA13: SWDIO
  PA2: USART2_TX          PA14: SWCLK / BOOT0
  PA3: USART2_RX          PB0: ADC1 ALERT/DRDY
  PA4: TPL5010 WAKE       PB1: ADC2 ALERT/DRDY
  PA5: TPL5010 DONE       PB3: LED R (sink)
  PB4: LED G (sink)       PB6: I2C1_SCL
  PB5: LED B (sink)       PB7: I2C1_SDA
  PC6: Excitation GPIO    PC7: PGOOD input
"""

#pragma experiment("BRIDGE_CONNECT")

import ElectricPower
import Electrical
import Resistor

from "protection.ato" import InputProtection
from "buck.ato" import BuckConverter
from "mcu.ato" import MCU
from "adc.ato" import ADCFrontEnd
from "rs485.ato" import RS485Bus
from "heater.ato" import HeaterDriver
from "led.ato" import StatusLED
from "connectors.ato" import Connectors
from "parts/onsemi_CAT24C32WI_GT3/onsemi_CAT24C32WI_GT3.ato" import onsemi_CAT24C32WI_GT3_package
from "parts/YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104/YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104.ato" import YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package

module SapFluxAdapter:
    """Top-level module for the sap flux sensor adapter board."""

    # === Power rails ===
    power_24v_raw = new ElectricPower
    power_24v_protected = new ElectricPower
    power_3v3 = new ElectricPower

    # === Shared I2C bus nodes ===
    sda = new Electrical
    scl = new Electrical

    # === Subsystem instances ===

    # Connectors (J1 M8 upstream, J2 10-pin sensor)
    connectors = new Connectors
    power_24v_raw ~ connectors.power_24v

    # Input protection (PTC + TVS + Schottky)
    input_protection = new InputProtection
    power_24v_raw ~ input_protection.power_in
    input_protection.power_out ~ power_24v_protected

    # Buck converter (24V -> 3.3V)
    buck = new BuckConverter
    power_24v_protected ~ buck.power_in
    buck.power_out ~ power_3v3

    # MCU
    mcu = new MCU
    power_3v3 ~ mcu.power

    # ADC front-end (2x ADS1115 + input protection + excitation filter)
    adc = new ADCFrontEnd
    power_3v3 ~ adc.power

    # RS-485 transceiver
    rs485 = new RS485Bus
    power_3v3 ~ rs485.power

    # Heater driver + TPL5010 watchdog + SCR latch
    heater = new HeaterDriver
    power_24v_protected ~ heater.power_24v
    power_3v3 ~ heater.power_3v3

    # Status LED
    led = new StatusLED
    power_3v3 ~ led.power

    # EEPROM (onsemi CAT24C32, SOIC-8, address 0x50)
    eeprom = new onsemi_CAT24C32WI_GT3_package
    c_eeprom = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package  # 100nF decoupling

    # === EEPROM wiring ===
    # Power + decoupling
    eeprom.VCC ~ power_3v3.hv
    eeprom.VSS ~ power_3v3.lv
    c_eeprom.p1 ~ power_3v3.hv
    c_eeprom.p2 ~ power_3v3.lv
    # I2C
    sda ~ eeprom.SDA
    scl ~ eeprom.SCL
    # Address = 0x50 (A0=A1=A2=GND)
    eeprom.A0 ~ power_3v3.lv
    eeprom.A1 ~ power_3v3.lv
    eeprom.A2 ~ power_3v3.lv
    # WP tied to GND (writes always allowed)
    eeprom.WP ~ power_3v3.lv

    # === I2C bus wiring ===
    # ADC front-end I2C
    sda ~ adc.sda
    scl ~ adc.scl

    # MCU I2C1 (PB7=SDA, PB6=SCL)
    sda ~ mcu.package.PB7
    scl ~ mcu.package.PB6

    # === RS-485 wiring ===
    # USART2 (PA2=TX, PA3=RX)
    mcu.package.PA2 ~ rs485.uart_tx
    mcu.package.PA3 ~ rs485.uart_rx
    # Control GPIOs (PA1=DE, PA0=~RE)
    mcu.package.PA1 ~ rs485.de
    mcu.package.PA0 ~ rs485.n_re
    # Bus lines to M8 connector
    rs485.rs485_a ~ connectors.rs485_a
    rs485.rs485_b ~ connectors.rs485_b

    # === Heater wiring ===
    # Gate drive from MCU timer (PA8 = TIM1_CH1, one-pulse mode)
    mcu.package.PA8 ~ heater.gate_drive
    # Watchdog I/O
    mcu.package.PA4 ~ heater.wake
    mcu.package.PA5 ~ heater.done
    # RSTn shared with MCU NRST
    mcu.nrst ~ heater.rstn
    # Heater terminals to J2 connector
    connectors.heater_hi ~ heater.heater_hi
    connectors.heater_lo ~ heater.heater_lo

    # === ADC wiring ===
    # Excitation GPIO (PC6)
    mcu.package.PC6 ~ adc.excitation_gpio
    # Excitation output to J2 connector
    adc.excitation_out ~ connectors.excitation
    # Thermistor lines from J2 to ADC
    connectors.thermistor_1 ~ adc.thermistor_1
    connectors.thermistor_2 ~ adc.thermistor_2
    connectors.thermistor_3 ~ adc.thermistor_3
    connectors.thermistor_4 ~ adc.thermistor_4
    connectors.thermistor_5 ~ adc.thermistor_5
    connectors.thermistor_6 ~ adc.thermistor_6
    # ALERT/DRDY to MCU (PB0=ADC1, PB1=ADC2)
    mcu.package.PB0 ~ adc.alert1
    mcu.package.PB1 ~ adc.alert2

    # === LED wiring ===
    # MCU sinks current (GPIOs drive low to turn on)
    mcu.package.PB3 ~ led.red
    mcu.package.PB4 ~ led.green
    mcu.package.PB5 ~ led.blue

    # === PGOOD monitoring ===
    # LM5165 PGOOD (open-drain) with 10k pull-up to 3.3V
    # Also gates SCR latch arming (prevents power-on reset from triggering latch)
    r_pgood = new Resistor
    r_pgood.resistance = 10kohm +/- 1%
    r_pgood.package = "0603"
    mcu.package.PC7 ~ buck.pgood.line
    buck.pgood.line ~> r_pgood ~> power_3v3.hv
    buck.pgood.line ~ heater.pgood

    # === Net name overrides (readable names in KiCad) ===
    # Workaround for atopile bug: override_net_name on ElectricPower.hv/.lv
    # is shadowed by the class's pre-existing SUGGESTED trait (try_get_trait
    # returns first match by insertion order). Standalone signals with
    # override_net_name are found by the net naming algorithm's hierarchy walk.
    signal V3V3 ~ power_3v3.hv
    V3V3.override_net_name = "V3V3"
    signal GND ~ power_3v3.lv
    GND.override_net_name = "GND"
    signal V24_RAW ~ power_24v_raw.hv
    V24_RAW.override_net_name = "V24_RAW"
    signal V24_PROT ~ power_24v_protected.hv
    V24_PROT.override_net_name = "V24_PROT"
    sda.override_net_name = "SDA"
    scl.override_net_name = "SCL"

--- FILE: elec/mcu.ato ---
"""
STM32G0B1CBT6 MCU module with power decoupling, BOOT0, NRST, and VDDA filtering.

Power topology:
  3.3V rail -> FB_VDDA (600 ohm ferrite bead) -> MCU VDD_VDDA, VBAT, VREFpos
  Bypass caps (4x 100nF) + bulk (1x 1uF) on MCU side of ferrite bead.

Note: LQFP-48 merges VDD and VDDA into one pin (VDD_VDDA). Ferrite bead
filters ALL MCU power. 200mA rating is ample for ~20mA MCU draw.

BOOT0: 10k pull-down to GND (normal boot from flash).
NRST: 100nF filter cap to GND. Exposed for TPL5010 RSTn connection.

GPIO assignments are made in the top-level module via package pin access.
"""

#pragma experiment("BRIDGE_CONNECT")

import Resistor
import ElectricPower
import Electrical

from "parts/STMicroelectronics_STM32G0B1CBT6/STMicroelectronics_STM32G0B1CBT6.ato" import STMicroelectronics_STM32G0B1CBT6_package
from "parts/Sunlord_GZ1608D601TF/Sunlord_GZ1608D601TF.ato" import Sunlord_GZ1608D601TF_package
from "parts/Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC/Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC.ato" import Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC_package
from "parts/YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104/YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104.ato" import YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package

module MCU:
    """
    STM32G0B1CBT6 with power filtering, decoupling, BOOT0 pull-down,
    and NRST filter cap.
    """

    # --- External interfaces ---
    power = new ElectricPower
    """3.3V supply rail (from buck converter)."""

    nrst = new Electrical
    """NRST node — exposed for TPL5010 RSTn + SCR latch connection."""

    # --- Package (exposed for GPIO wiring in top-level) ---
    package = new STMicroelectronics_STM32G0B1CBT6_package

    # --- VDDA ferrite bead ---
    fb_vdda = new Sunlord_GZ1608D601TF_package
    """600 ohm @ 100MHz. Filters digital noise from MCU power pins."""

    # --- Internal filtered rail node (named signal for readable net name) ---

    # --- Bulk cap on VDDA (1uF, after ferrite bead) ---
    c_vdda = new Samsung_Electro_Mechanics_CL10A105KB8NNNC_package

    # --- Bypass caps (4x 100nF, after ferrite bead) ---
    c_mcu1 = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
    c_mcu2 = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
    c_mcu3 = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
    c_mcu4 = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package

    # --- NRST filter cap ---
    c_nrst = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package

    # --- BOOT0 pull-down ---
    r_boot0 = new Resistor
    r_boot0.resistance = 10kohm +/- 1%
    r_boot0.package = "0603"

    # === Power path: 3.3V -> ferrite bead -> MCU pins ===
    power.hv ~ fb_vdda.p1
    signal VDDA_FILT ~ fb_vdda.p2
    VDDA_FILT.override_net_name = "VDDA_FILT"

    # MCU power pins (all on filtered side)
    VDDA_FILT ~ package.VDD_VDDA
    VDDA_FILT ~ package.VBAT
    VDDA_FILT ~ package.VREFpos
    power.lv ~ package.VSS_VSSA

    # === Bypass caps (after ferrite bead) ===
    VDDA_FILT ~ c_mcu1.p1
    c_mcu1.p2 ~ power.lv

    VDDA_FILT ~ c_mcu2.p1
    c_mcu2.p2 ~ power.lv

    VDDA_FILT ~ c_mcu3.p1
    c_mcu3.p2 ~ power.lv

    VDDA_FILT ~ c_mcu4.p1
    c_mcu4.p2 ~ power.lv

    # === VDDA bulk cap (after ferrite bead) ===
    VDDA_FILT ~ c_vdda.p1
    c_vdda.p2 ~ power.lv

    # === NRST ===
    package.PF2_NRST ~ nrst
    nrst ~ c_nrst.p1
    c_nrst.p2 ~ power.lv

    # === BOOT0 pull-down ===
    signal BOOT0 ~ package.PA14_BOOT0
    BOOT0 ~> r_boot0 ~> power.lv

--- FILE: elec/protection.ato ---
"""
Input protection circuit: PTC fuse + TVS clamp + Schottky reverse polarity.

Topology:
  J1 (24V) --> F1 (PTC) --> node_a --> D1 (Schottky, anode->cathode) --> +24V Protected
                                |
                              D2 (TVS, cathode to node_a, anode to GND)
                                |
                               GND
"""

import Electrical
import ElectricPower

from "parts/Littelfuse_2920L110_60MR/Littelfuse_2920L110_60MR.ato" import Littelfuse_2920L110_60MR_package
from "parts/FTR_SMAJ33A/FTR_SMAJ33A.ato" import FTR_SMAJ33A_package
from "parts/MDD_Microdiode_Electronics_SS36/MDD_Microdiode_Electronics_SS36.ato" import MDD_Microdiode_Electronics_SS36_package

module InputProtection:
    """
    24V input protection: PTC fuse (1.1A hold, 60V),
    TVS clamp (33V standoff, ~53V clamp), Schottky reverse polarity (60V/3A).
    """

    # External interfaces
    power_in = new ElectricPower
    power_out = new ElectricPower

    # Components
    f1 = new Littelfuse_2920L110_60MR_package
    d2_tvs = new FTR_SMAJ33A_package
    d1_schottky = new MDD_Microdiode_Electronics_SS36_package

    # Internal node between fuse output and diodes
    node_a = new Electrical

    # F1: series fuse from input to node_a
    power_in.hv ~ f1.p1
    f1.p2 ~ node_a

    # D2: TVS clamp, cathode to node_a, anode to GND
    d2_tvs.C ~ node_a
    d2_tvs.A ~ power_in.lv

    # D1: Schottky, anode to node_a, cathode to output
    d1_schottky.A ~ node_a
    d1_schottky.K ~ power_out.hv

    # Ground passthrough
    power_in.lv ~ power_out.lv

--- FILE: elec/rs485.ato ---
"""
RS-485 transceiver: SP3485 + AC termination + SM712 TVS + boot pull-ups/downs.

Topology:
  MCU UART TX → SP3485 DI
  MCU UART RX ← SP3485 RO
  MCU GPIO DE → SP3485 DE (R_DE_PD 100k pull-down: driver OFF during boot)
  MCU GPIO ~RE → SP3485 ~RE (R_RE_PD 100k pull-down: receiver ON during boot)

  SP3485 A/B → SM712 TVS → M8 connector (via top-level wiring)
  A-B: R_TERM (120 ohm) + C_TERM (100nF) in series (AC termination)

No bias resistors — SP3485 fail-safe receiver handles floating bus.
"""

#pragma experiment("BRIDGE_CONNECT")

import Resistor
import ElectricPower
import Electrical

from "atopile/maxlinear-sp3485/maxlinear-sp3485.ato" import MaxLinear_SP3485
from "parts/hongjiacheng_SM712/hongjiacheng_SM712.ato" import hongjiacheng_SM712_package
from "parts/YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104/YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104.ato" import YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package

module RS485Bus:
    """
    SP3485 half-duplex RS-485 transceiver with AC termination,
    SM712 TVS protection, and boot-safe pull resistors.
    """

    # --- External interfaces ---
    power = new ElectricPower
    """3.3V supply."""

    uart_tx = new Electrical
    """MCU UART TX → SP3485 DI (data in)."""

    uart_rx = new Electrical
    """MCU UART RX ← SP3485 RO (receiver out)."""

    de = new Electrical
    """MCU GPIO → SP3485 DE (driver enable, active high)."""

    n_re = new Electrical
    """MCU GPIO → SP3485 ~RE (receiver enable, active low)."""

    rs485_a = new Electrical
    """RS-485 A line (to M8 connector)."""

    rs485_b = new Electrical
    """RS-485 B line (to M8 connector)."""

    # --- SP3485 transceiver (registry: includes 100nF decoupling) ---
    transceiver = new MaxLinear_SP3485
    power ~ transceiver.power

    # UART connections
    uart_tx ~ transceiver.uart.tx.line
    uart_rx ~ transceiver.uart.rx.line

    # Control lines
    de ~ transceiver.driver_enable.line
    n_re ~ transceiver.n_receiver_enable.line

    # RS-485 bus
    rs485_a ~ transceiver.rs485_bus.p.line
    rs485_b ~ transceiver.rs485_bus.n.line

    # --- Boot-state pull resistors (100k, auto-pick) ---
    r_de_pd = new Resistor
    r_de_pd.resistance = 100kohm +/- 1%
    r_de_pd.package = "0603"

    r_re_pd = new Resistor
    r_re_pd.resistance = 100kohm +/- 1%
    r_re_pd.package = "0603"

    # DE pull-down: driver OFF during boot (Hi-Z GPIOs)
    de ~> r_de_pd ~> power.lv

    # ~RE pull-down: receiver ON during boot (enables USART wakeup from Stop)
    n_re ~> r_re_pd ~> power.lv

    # --- AC termination (120 ohm + 100nF in series between A and B) ---
    r_term = new Resistor
    r_term.resistance = 120ohm +/- 1%
    r_term.package = "0603"

    c_term = new YAGEO_CC0603KRX7R9BB104_package
    """100nF 50V. Blocks DC, terminates signal edges. |Z| = 123 ohm at 115200 baud."""

    signal RS485_TERM
    rs485_a ~> r_term ~> RS485_TERM
    RS485_TERM ~ c_term.p1
    c_term.p2 ~ rs485_b

    # --- SM712 TVS (asymmetric dual, purpose-built for RS-485) ---
    d_rs485 = new hongjiacheng_SM712_package
    """7V/12V standoff, 16V/26V clamp. Place near M8 connector."""

    d_rs485.A ~ rs485_a
    d_rs485.B ~ rs485_b
    d_rs485.GND ~ power.lv

def update_layers(content):
    """Add inner copper layers for 4-layer stackup."""
    # Add In1.Cu and In2.Cu after B.Cu line
    content = content.replace(
        '\t\t(31 "B.Cu" signal)',
        '\t\t(1 "In1.Cu" signal "GND")\n\t\t(2 "In2.Cu" signal "3V3")\n\t\t(31 "B.Cu" signal)'
    )
    return content


def update_stackup(content):
    """Update stackup to 4-layer with proper dielectrics."""
    old_stackup = '''		(layer "F.Cu"
			(type "copper")
			(thickness 0.035)
		)
		(layer "dielectric 1"
			(type "core")
			(thickness 1.51)
			(material "FR4")
			(epsilon_r 4.5)
			(loss_tangent 0.02)
		)
		(layer "B.Cu"
			(type "copper")
			(thickness 0.035)
		)'''

    new_stackup = '''		(layer "F.Cu"
			(type "copper")
			(thickness 0.035)
		)
		(layer "dielectric 1"
			(type "prepreg")
			(thickness 0.21)
			(material "FR4")
			(epsilon_r 4.5)
			(loss_tangent 0.02)
		)
		(layer "In1.Cu"
			(type "copper")
			(thickness 0.0175)
		)
		(layer "dielectric 2"
			(type "core")
			(thickness 1.065)
			(material "FR4")
			(epsilon_r 4.5)
			(loss_tangent 0.02)
		)
		(layer "In2.Cu"
			(type "copper")
			(thickness 0.0175)
		)
		(layer "dielectric 3"
			(type "prepreg")
			(thickness 0.21)
			(material "FR4")
			(epsilon_r 4.5)
			(loss_tangent 0.02)
		)
		(layer "B.Cu"
			(type "copper")
			(thickness 0.035)
		)'''

    content = content.replace(old_stackup, new_stackup)
    return content


def place_components(content):
    """Update component positions based on atopile_address mapping."""
    placed = set()
    not_found = []

    for addr, (x, y, rot) in PLACEMENTS.items():
        # Find the footprint block containing this atopile_address
        # Pattern: "atopile_address" "<addr>"
        pattern = f'"atopile_address" "{addr}"'
        idx = content.find(pattern)
        if idx == -1:
            not_found.append(addr)
            continue

        # Find the start of this footprint block (search backwards for "(footprint")
        fp_start = content.rfind("(footprint", 0, idx)
        if fp_start == -1:
            not_found.append(addr)
            continue

        # Find the (at X Y rotation) within this footprint block
        # Search from fp_start to some reasonable distance
        fp_section = content[fp_start:fp_start + 2000]

        # Match (at X Y) or (at X Y rotation)
        at_match = re.search(r'\(at (-?[\d.]+) (-?[\d.]+)( -?[\d.]+)?\)', fp_section)
        if at_match:
            old_at = at_match.group(0)
            if rot == 0:
                new_at = f"(at {x} {y})"
            else:
                new_at = f"(at {x} {y} {rot})"

            # Replace in the original content (only first occurrence from fp_start)
            old_pos = content.find(old_at, fp_start)
            if old_pos != -1 and old_pos < fp_start + 2000:
                content = content[:old_pos] + new_at + content[old_pos + len(old_at):]
                placed.add(addr)
            else:
                not_found.append(addr)
        else:
            not_found.append(addr)

    print(f"Placed {len(placed)} components")
    if not_found:
        print(f"NOT FOUND ({len(not_found)}): {not_found}")
    return content


def remove_traces(content):
    """Remove all auto-generated segments and vias."""
    # Remove segment lines
    content = re.sub(r'\t\(segment\n(?:\t\t[^\n]+\n)+\t\)\n', '', content)
    # Also try single-line segments
    content = re.sub(r'\t\(segment [^\n]+\n', '', content)
    # Remove vias
    content = re.sub(r'\t\(via\n(?:\t\t[^\n]+\n)+\t\)\n', '', content)
    content = re.sub(r'\t\(via [^\n]+\n', '', content)
    return content


def add_board_outline(content):
    """Add Edge.Cuts board outline rectangle."""
    outline = f'''
	(gr_rect
		(start 100 50)
		(end 190 112)
		(stroke
			(width 0.05)
			(type default)
		)
		(fill none)
		(layer "Edge.Cuts")
		(uuid "{gen_uuid()}")
	)
'''
    # Insert before the closing paren of the file
    content = content.rstrip()
    if content.endswith(')'):
        content = content[:-1] + outline + ')\n'
    return content


def add_mounting_holes(content):
    """Add 4x M3 mounting holes."""
    positions = [(104, 54), (186, 54), (104, 108), (186, 108)]
    holes = ""
    for i, (x, y) in enumerate(positions):
        holes += f'''
	(footprint "MountingHole:MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad"
		(layer "F.Cu")
		(uuid "{gen_uuid()}")
		(at {x} {y})
		(property "Reference" "MH{i+1}"
			(at 0 -3.5)
			(layer "F.SilkS")
			(uuid "{gen_uuid()}")
			(effects
				(font
					(size 1 1)
					(thickness 0.15)
				)
			)
		)
		(property "Value" "MountingHole"
			(at 0 3.5)
			(layer "F.Fab")
			(uuid "{gen_uuid()}")
			(effects
				(font
					(size 1 1)
					(thickness 0.15)
				)
			)
		)
		(pad "1" thru_hole circle
			(at 0 0)
			(size 6 6)
			(drill 3.2)
			(layers "*.Cu" "*.Mask")
			(net 73 "lv")
			(uuid "{gen_uuid()}")
		)
	)
'''
    content = content.rstrip()
    if content.endswith(')'):
        content = content[:-1] + holes + ')\n'
    return content


def add_fiducials(content):
    """Add 3x fiducial markers."""
    positions = [(104, 52), (188, 52), (104, 110)]
    fids = ""
    for i, (x, y) in enumerate(positions):
        fids += f'''
	(footprint "Fiducial:Fiducial_1mm_Mask2mm"
		(layer "F.Cu")
		(uuid "{gen_uuid()}")
		(at {x} {y})
		(property "Reference" "FID{i+1}"
			(at 0 -2)
			(layer "F.SilkS")
			(uuid "{gen_uuid()}")
			(effects
				(font
					(size 0.8 0.8)
					(thickness 0.1)
				)
			)
		)
		(property "Value" "Fiducial"
			(at 0 2)
			(layer "F.Fab")
			(uuid "{gen_uuid()}")
			(effects
				(font
					(size 0.8 0.8)
					(thickness 0.1)
				)
			)
		)
		(pad "1" smd circle
			(at 0 0)
			(size 1 1)
			(layers "F.Cu" "F.Mask")
			(solder_mask_margin 0.5)
			(uuid "{gen_uuid()}")
		)
	)
'''
    content = content.rstrip()
    if content.endswith(')'):
        content = content[:-1] + fids + ')\n'
    return content


def add_zones(content):
    """Add GND and 3.3V copper zone fills."""
    # GND zone on In1.Cu - covers entire board
    gnd_zone = f'''
	(zone
		(net 73)
		(net_name "lv")
		(layer "In1.Cu")
		(uuid "{gen_uuid()}")
		(hatch edge 0.5)
		(connect_pads
			(clearance 0.3)
		)
		(min_thickness 0.2)
		(fill yes
			(thermal_gap 0.3)
			(thermal_bridge_width 0.3)
		)
		(polygon
			(pts
				(xy 100 50) (xy 190 50) (xy 190 112) (xy 100 112)
			)
		)
	)
'''
    # 3.3V zone on In2.Cu - covers MCU + ADC + digital area (right 2/3 of board)
    v33_zone = f'''
	(zone
		(net 74)
		(net_name "power_out-hv")
		(layer "In2.Cu")
		(uuid "{gen_uuid()}")
		(hatch edge 0.5)
		(connect_pads
			(clearance 0.3)
		)
		(min_thickness 0.2)
		(fill yes
			(thermal_gap 0.3)
			(thermal_bridge_width 0.3)
		)
		(polygon
			(pts
				(xy 120 50) (xy 190 50) (xy 190 100) (xy 120 100)
			)
		)
	)
'''
    # GND zone on B.Cu - entire board (secondary ground fill)
    gnd_bcu = f'''
	(zone
		(net 73)
		(net_name "lv")
		(layer "B.Cu")
		(uuid "{gen_uuid()}")
		(hatch edge 0.5)
		(connect_pads
			(clearance 0.3)
		)
		(min_thickness 0.2)
		(fill yes
			(thermal_gap 0.3)
			(thermal_bridge_width 0.3)
		)
		(polygon
			(pts
				(xy 100 50) (xy 190 50) (xy 190 112) (xy 100 112)
			)
		)
	)
'''

    content = content.rstrip()
    if content.endswith(')'):
        content = content[:-1] + gnd_zone + v33_zone + gnd_bcu + ')\n'
    return content


def main():
    with open(PCB_PATH, 'r') as f:
        content = f.read()

    print(f"Read {len(content)} chars, {content.count(chr(10))} lines")

    # Step 1: Update layers for 4-layer
    content = update_layers(content)
    print("Updated layers to 4-layer")

    # Step 2: Update stackup
    content = update_stackup(content)
    print("Updated stackup")

    # Step 3: Remove existing auto-traces
    before = content.count('(segment')
    content = remove_traces(content)
    after = content.count('(segment')
    print(f"Removed traces: {before} -> {after} segments remaining")

    # Step 4: Place components
    content = place_components(content)

    # Step 5: Add board outline
    content = add_board_outline(content)
    print("Added board outline")

    # Step 6: Add mounting holes
    content = add_mounting_holes(content)
    print("Added mounting holes")

    # Step 7: Add fiducials
    content = add_fiducials(content)
    print("Added fiducials")

    # Step 8: Add zones
    content = add_zones(content)
    print("Added zone fills")

    with open(PCB_PATH, 'w') as f:
        f.write(content)

    print(f"\nWrote {len(content)} chars to {PCB_PATH}")
    print("Done! Open in KiCad to verify.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

--- FILE: proposed_v1.1_revisions.md ---
# Proposed v1.1 Revisions

Changes for the next board revision. v1.0 design documented in
`riley_design.md`. All part numbers verified against JLCPCB stock
as of 2026-02-26.

**v1.0 baseline:** 39 BOM lines, 83 components, ~$116 for 5 boards.

**v1.1 vision:** Scale from a single East30 sensor to **up to 12
sap flux probes** (48 thermistor channels) off one logic board. Target
cost: ~$100/plot for 8-12 tree coverage. 71x cheaper than commercial
alternatives (~$1,375/tree).

---

## 1. RTC Crystal + Software Temperature Compensation

**Goal:** Autonomous timekeeping with <5 min/year drift when not
connected to a logger.

**Parts to add:**
- Q13FC13500004 (C32346) -- 32.768 kHz crystal, +/-20 ppm, SMD3215-2P,
  basic (no setup fee), $0.18, 659K stock, CL = 12.5 pF
- 2x FH 0402CG180J500NT (C1549) -- 18 pF C0G/NP0 50V, 0402,
  **basic** (no setup fee), $0.001 each, 1.5M stock.
  18 pF gives CL = 12.0 pF assuming 3 pF stray. STM32 RTC CALR
  calibration register compensates +/-488 ppm, so exact cap value is
  non-critical. Tune after first board bring-up if desired.

**Firmware:**
- One-time frequency calibration using STM32 RTC smooth calibration
  register (+/-488 ppm range, 0.954 ppm steps). Eliminates initial
  +/-20 ppm crystal tolerance.
- Software temperature compensation using STM32 internal die temp
  sensor (+/-1.5C). Crystal parabolic model:
  delta_f/f = -0.034 ppm/C^2 * (T - 25)^2
- RS-485 time sync from logger when connected (eliminates long-term drift).

**Expected accuracy:** ~1.3 min/year worst case (0C winter), ~0.3 min/year
at typical forest temps (10-30C). No dedicated crystal temp sensor needed --
MCU sleeps 99.3% of the time so die temp ~= ambient.

**MCU pins:** PC14 (OSC32_IN), PC15 (OSC32_OUT) -- dedicated RTC crystal
pins, no conflict with existing assignments.

**Layout constraints:** Crystal traces < 5 mm. Ground guard ring around
crystal and traces. No switching signals (SPI, mux select, heater gate)
nearby. Load caps placed symmetrically, close to crystal pads.

---

## 2. ADC Architecture: Triple Mux, 48 Thermistor Channels

**Goal:** Support up to 12 sap flux probes (4 thermistors each = 48
channels) with a single ADS1115, using three cascaded 16:1 analog muxes.

**Change:** Remove one ADS1115. Add 3x 74HC4067 16:1 analog muxes.
All thermistor lines route through muxes into ADS1115 AIN0. Excitation
sense goes directly to AIN1 (single-ended ratiometric measurement).

| | v1.0 (2x ADS1115) | v1.1 (1x ADS1115 + 3x mux) |
|---|---|---|
| ADC chips | 2 | 1 |
| Max thermistors | 6 | 48 (3x 16-channel mux) |
| Resolution | 16-bit | 16-bit (same ADC) |
| Interface | I2C | I2C + 4 GPIO (shared select) + 3 GPIO (enables) |
| Idle power | 1 uA | 0.5 uA + ~0 (mux is CMOS, nA leakage) |
| Price delta | -- | +$0.41 (drop ADC + passives, add 3x mux) |

### Mux part

74HC4067PW,118 (C179326) -- Nexperia, 16:1, 80 ohm Ron, TSSOP-24,
31K stock, $0.57 each, extended. Qty 3.

### How it works

Three muxes share select lines S0-S3 (4 GPIOs). Each mux has its own
enable pin (~E, active low). Only one mux is enabled at a time:

```
Thermistors 1-16  → Mux A (channels 0-15) → ──┐
                                                │
Thermistors 17-32 → Mux B (channels 0-15) → ──┼→ ADS1115 AIN0
                                                │
Thermistors 33-48 → Mux C (channels 0-15) → ──┘
```

Firmware cycle: set S0-S3 → enable mux A (disable B, C) → start ADC →
read result → next channel. After mux A channel 15, switch to mux B,
then mux C.

Enable toggling prevents crosstalk: the disabled muxes' outputs are
high-impedance, so charge injection from their channels can't corrupt
the active measurement.

### Single excitation line

One GPIO pin (PC6) drives all 48 thermistor half-bridges through a
single RC filter:

- R_EXC = 270 ohm (C22966, UNI-ROYAL 0603WAF2700T5E, basic, $0.001)
- C_EXC = 1 uF (C15849, existing BOM)
- Filter cutoff: fc = 1 / (2 * pi * 270 * 1e-6) = 589 Hz

At 12 sensors (48 half-bridges, 20k each @ 25°C): R_load = 417 ohm.
V_exc = 3.3 * 417 / (417 + 270) = 2.00V. I_steady = 4.8 mA.
I_inrush = 3.3 / 270 = 12.2 mA (safe, under STM32 20 mA GPIO limit).

Firmware: enable PC6 before scan, read all 48 mux channels across
all three muxes, disable PC6. Simpler than dual-excitation (no per-group
enable/disable sequencing).

### Excitation sense: ratiometric on AIN1

The single excitation line connects to AIN1 through a 1k series
resistor + 100 nF filter cap (matching the thermistor path protection).
Firmware reads excitation as a **separate single-ended conversion**
(AINp=AIN1, AINn=GND) once per scan cycle, then divides each
thermistor reading by excitation to get ratiometric values:

  T = steinhart_hart(V_therm / V_exc)

Ratiometric measurement cancels excitation voltage uncertainty
(GPIO output variation, R_EXC voltage divider, supply noise). The
2.00V excitation at 48 channels is not a problem — only the ratio
matters. See Section 12 (Sensor Topology) for detailed analysis of
excitation depression and the critical firmware requirement to
measure V_exc rather than assume 3.3V.

This loses hardware differential CMRR vs v1.0, but:

- Ground bounce is already managed (no ADC during heater pulses)
- Common-mode noise during quiescent reads is minimal (no switching)
- Avoids adding an analog switch IC (saves BOM complexity)
- Temperature differencing (heated - reference) cancels remaining
  systematic errors

AIN2, AIN3: tied to AGND through 1k resistors (prevent noise coupling).

### Scan rates and noise

ADS1115 data rates and noise (PGA = +/-4.096V, LSB = 125 uV):

| Data Rate | Conversion Time | Noise (uVrms) | Temp Noise (mC) | 48-ch Scan | Scan Rate |
|-----------|----------------|---------------|-----------------|------------|-----------|
| 8 SPS | 125 ms | 7.8 | 0.3 | 6.18 s | 0.2 Hz |
| 16 SPS | 62.5 ms | 11 | 0.4 | 3.12 s | 0.3 Hz |
| 32 SPS | 31.3 ms | 16 | 0.5 | 1.59 s | 0.6 Hz |
| 64 SPS | 15.6 ms | 23 | 0.8 | 0.82 s | 1.2 Hz |
| 128 SPS | 7.81 ms | 31 | 1.0 | 0.44 s | 2.3 Hz |
| 250 SPS | 4.0 ms | 47 | 1.6 | 0.25 s | 4.0 Hz |
| 475 SPS | 2.1 ms | 64 | 2.1 | 0.16 s | 6.3 Hz |
| 860 SPS | 1.16 ms | 94 | 3.1 | 0.11 s | 8.9 Hz |

**Temp noise** uses sensitivity of 30.2 mV/°C at 25°C (Curve 44 NTC
with 10kΩ R_ref). See Section 12 for derivation.

**Note:** Each channel requires a dummy conversion after mux switch
(ADS1115 sampling cap needs to settle). Use fast-dummy trick: run
dummy at 860 SPS (1.16 ms), real conversion at desired SPS. This adds
only 1.16 ms overhead per channel instead of doubling scan time.

**Derivative noise insight:** For sap flux, we measure dT/dt. Derivative
noise = sqrt(2) * temp_noise / dt. Faster scanning is NOT always better
for derivatives -- the noise/dt term grows. Sweet spot: 64-250 SPS.

### Adaptive scan strategy

| Phase | Time Window | Data Rate | 48-ch Rate | Purpose |
|-------|------------|-----------|------------|---------|
| Fast (heating) | 0-5 s | 860 SPS | 8.9 Hz | Capture initial transient |
| Medium | 5-30 s | 250 SPS | 4.0 Hz | Track decay curve |
| Slow (tail) | 30-120 s | 64 SPS | 1.2 Hz | High-precision baseline |

Alternative: always collect at 860 SPS (max speed), filter in software.
Trades flash storage (~100 KB/cycle at 860 SPS, 48 ch) for simplicity.
At 32 MB flash: ~328 cycles = ~7 days. Adaptive mode recommended.

### Supported sensor configurations

| Config | Thermistors | Mux A | Mux B | Mux C | 860 SPS Rate |
|--------|-------------|-------|-------|-------|-------------|
| 1x East30 (4-pin) | 4 | 4 ch | idle | idle | 96 Hz |
| 2x East30 | 8 | 8 ch | idle | idle | 51 Hz |
| 4x East30 | 16 | 16 ch | idle | idle | 26 Hz |
| 8x East30 (4-pin) | 32 | 16 ch | 16 ch | idle | 13 Hz |
| 8x 6-pin probes | 48 | 16 ch | 16 ch | 16 ch | 8.9 Hz |
| 12x East30 (4-pin) | 48 | 16 ch | 16 ch | 16 ch | 8.9 Hz |

Rates assume 2 conversions per mux channel (dummy + real for settling)
plus 1 excitation read per scan cycle.

### MCU pins for mux

| Pin | Function | Notes |
|-----|----------|-------|
| PD0 | Mux select S0 | Shared between all three muxes |
| PD1 | Mux select S1 | Shared |
| PD2 | Mux select S2 | Shared |
| PD3 | Mux select S3 | Shared |
| PA9 | Mux A enable (~E) | Active low. 10k pull-up to 3.3V (boot-safe: mux disabled). |
| PA10 | Mux B enable (~E) | Active low. 10k pull-up to 3.3V (boot-safe: mux disabled). |
| PA11 | Mux C enable (~E) | Active low. 10k pull-up to 3.3V (boot-safe: mux disabled). |

PB1 freed (was ADC2 ALERT/DRDY in v1.0).

---

## 3. 32 MB NOR Flash

**Goal:** Autonomous data logging for 6-12 months when not connected to
a logger.

**Part:** W25Q256JVFIQ (C779876)
- 32 MB (256 Mbit), SPI, SOIC-16
- 1 uA typical standby / 10 uA max
- Deep power-down: 0.5 uA typical (enter via SPI command between cycles)
- 100K erase cycles, 20-year retention
- $3.92 (qty 10+; $4.26 qty 1), 28K stock, extended

**Pin notes (SOIC-16):**
- Pin 1 RESET#/IO3: tie to VCC (quad-SPI not used; also serves as /HOLD)
- Pin 2 VCC: 3.3V + 100 nF decoupling cap (C14663, existing part)
- Pin 3 RESET#: tie to VCC (active-low reset, keep deasserted)
- Pins 4-6, 11-14: N/C
- Pin 7 CS#: PB12 + 10k pull-up to VCC (boot-safe: flash deselected
  while MCU GPIOs are high-Z during reset)
- Pin 8 DO/IO1: PB14 (MISO)
- Pin 9 WP#/IO2: tie to VCC (no hardware write-protect needed)
- Pin 10 GND
- Pin 15 DI/IO0: PB15 (MOSI)
- Pin 16 CLK: PB13 (SCK)

**Data budget (int16 storage, adaptive scan for 120 s after each 2 s
heater pulse, 30-min intervals, 48 channels):**

| Item | Size |
|------|------|
| Per sample | 48 ch x 2 bytes = 96 bytes |
| Per measurement cycle (adaptive) | ~167 scans x 96 B + 8 B header = ~16 KB |
| Per measurement cycle (860 SPS constant) | ~1,063 scans x 96 B = ~100 KB |
| Per day (48 cycles, adaptive) | ~752 KB |
| 32 MB capacity (adaptive) | ~44 days at 48 ch |
| With 4 channels (1 probe, adaptive) | ~48 days (more scans, similar cycle size) |

Note: per-cycle storage is roughly independent of channel count (~16 KB).
More channels = slower scans = fewer samples, but larger samples. The
product is nearly constant. Storage scales with cycles/day, not channels.

Adaptive scan: 860 SPS x 5s (44 scans) + 250 SPS x 25s (64 scans) +
64 SPS x 90s (59 scans) = ~167 scans per cycle. At constant 860 SPS:
~1,063 scans/cycle (~100 KB) = ~7 days at 48 ch.

**MCU pins:** SPI2 bus (PB13=SCK, PB14=MISO, PB15=MOSI) + PB12 (CS).
SPI1 is blocked -- PA5 (SPI1_SCK) is already used by TPL5010 DONE.

---

## 4. Connector Topology, Multi-Heater Support & Gate Driver

**Goal:** Support 1-8 heater probes with safe, efficient high-current
switching. Anti-footgun design: safe at any pulse duration, any number
of heaters.

### Connector layout: two separate blocks on the same board edge

**Heater block (2-pin):** KF2EDGV-3.5-2P (C441321)
- Pin 1: Heater+ (24V switched)
- Pin 2: Heater- (drain return)
- $0.06, 11K stock, extended
- Width: 7 mm

Users wire 1-8 heater elements in parallel at the cable level. The
board just provides switched 24V. Each heater is ~42 ohm, so 8 in
parallel = 5.25 ohm = 4.57 A total.

**Thermistor/signal block:** 2x30 pin header (60P), XKB X6521WV-2x30H-C60D30
(C2883964), $0.96, extended.
- 48 thermistor inputs (3x 16-channel mux groups)
- GND (thermistor ground return, multiple pins for crosstalk isolation)
- Excitation (GPIO-switched 3.3V via 270 ohm filter)
- See Section 11 for full pinout.

**Auxiliary header:** 1x6 pin header (2.54mm), for I2C bus, common
ground, and spare GPIOs. Separate from the thermistor connector to
avoid mixing digital signals with precision analog lines.
- I2C SDA + SCL (through 1k on-board series protection resistors)
- GND x2 (common ground reference for external devices)
- Spare GPIO x2 (PA6, PA7)
- No 3.3V export (buck headroom too tight, see Section 13 FAQ).
  External devices bring their own power.

Total connector edge footprint: ~90 mm. Fits on 100mm board edge.

**Why separate blocks:**
- Physical isolation of high-current (4.57 A) heater path from
  microvolt-level thermistor signals
- Can disconnect heater cable without disturbing thermistor wiring
- Simpler cable assemblies (power wires are thicker gauge)
- Standard 2.54mm pin headers are rated 3A per pin — insufficient for
  8-heater current (4.57A). The screw terminal handles it with margin
  (10A rating). Thermistor signals are ~60 µA each — 5,000x below the
  pin header's 3A rating.

### Gate driver circuit (NEW in v1.1)

The v1.0 design drives the heater MOSFET gate directly from a 3.3V
MCU GPIO. At v1.1 currents (up to 4.57A for 8 heaters), even a
low-Vgs(th) MOSFET at 3.3V gate has significant Rds(on) and wastes
heat. A gate driver boosts gate voltage to 10V from the existing
24V rail, dropping Rds(on) to spec-sheet values.

**Critical safety requirement (buck-dead fail-safe):** If the 3.3V
buck fails (IC failure, inductor open, output short) while 24V is
still present, the heater MUST remain OFF. Earlier revisions biased
Q_DRIVER from the 3.3V rail (R_PA8_PU), which made all four safety
layers (MCU timer, IWDG, TPL5010, SCR latch) dependent on 3.3V.
If the buck dies, all four fail simultaneously and R_GATE_PULL
charges Q1 gate to 10V with nothing to stop it — heater ON
indefinitely. The current design eliminates this by biasing Q_DRIVER
from the 24V rail via a voltage divider, with PA8 isolated through
Q_CTRL to avoid STM32 ESD clamp back-feed.

**Circuit:**

```
                    R_GATE_PULL (1M)                            Node A
V24_PROT ──────────────────────────────┬───────── Q1 Gate
                                       │
                            D_ZENER (10V, cathode at A, anode to GND)
                                       │
                            Q_DRIVER (drain at A, source to GND)

Q_DRIVER gate: 24V-biased always-on
    V24_PROT ── R_BIAS (4.7M) ──┬── Q_DRIVER gate ── R_GATE_PD (1M) ── GND
                                 │
                            Q_CTRL drain
                            Q_CTRL source ── GND

Q_CTRL gate: MCU-controlled
    PA8 (MCU) ── R_CTRL (10k) ── Q_CTRL gate ── R_CTRL_PD (100k) ── GND
```

**How it works (normal operation):**
1. PA8 LOW → Q_CTRL OFF → Q_DRIVER gate at 4.2V (24V divider) →
   Q_DRIVER ON → drain at ~0V → Q1 gate at ~0V → **heater OFF**
2. PA8 HIGH → Q_CTRL ON → Q_DRIVER gate pulled to ~0V → Q_DRIVER
   OFF → R_GATE_PULL pulls Q1 gate toward 24V → D_ZENER clamps at
   10V → **heater ON** at full Rds(on) spec

**Non-inverted logic (PA8 HIGH = heater ON).** Same polarity as
v1.0. Firmware drives PA8 LOW (default) to keep heater off, then
briefly drives PA8 HIGH for the 2-second heater pulse.

**Why Q_CTRL isolation is required:** An earlier revision connected
PA8 directly to Q_DRIVER gate through a resistor (R_GATE_DRV). The
24V divider on Q_DRIVER gate works correctly in steady state, but
during boot or buck-dead scenarios (V3V3 = 0V), the STM32's internal
ESD protection diode on PA8 forward-biases to VDD, sinking current
from the 24V divider node into the unpowered 3.3V rail. With
R_GATE_DRV = 100k, this pulls Q_DRIVER gate below Vgs(th) (0.99V
vs 1.5V threshold) — defeating the fail-safe in exactly the scenario
it's meant to protect. Increasing R_GATE_DRV doesn't help: values
large enough to limit ESD current (>470k) also prevent PA8 from
overriding the divider to control Q_DRIVER. Q_CTRL breaks this
impasse by isolating PA8 from the divider entirely.

**Boot behavior (24V divider provides fail-safe Q_DRIVER bias):**

R_BIAS (4.7M) and R_GATE_PD (1M) form a voltage divider from
V24_PROT to GND. This is purely resistive — responds instantly to
V24 rising, independent of the 3.3V rail.

1. Power applied. V24_PROT rises. Divider immediately biases
   Q_DRIVER gate at V24 × 1M/5.7M. When V24 reaches ~8.6V (typ
   Vgs(th) = 1.5V × 5.7), Q_DRIVER turns ON → Q1 gate clamped
   to ~0V.
2. R_CTRL_PD (100k) holds Q_CTRL gate at 0V → Q_CTRL OFF → does
   not interfere with Q_DRIVER bias.
3. Buck starts (V24 > ~3.5V UVLO). V3V3 ramps to 3.3V.
4. MCU boots. PA8 defaults to input (high-Z) → Q_CTRL stays OFF →
   Q_DRIVER stays ON → heater stays OFF. No glitch.
5. Only after firmware explicitly drives PA8 HIGH can heater turn ON.

**Boot glitch: none (battery hot-plug).** For step-function V24
(battery connect), the resistive divider biases Q_DRIVER ON
before R_GATE_PULL (1M, τ = 1.8ms) can charge Q1 gate past
Vgs(th). No heater conduction during boot. This is an improvement
over the previous ~1ms glitch.

**Slow-ramp note (solar sunrise):** During a gradual V24 ramp (0V
to 24V over minutes), there is a brief window between V24 ≈ 2.5V
(Q1 Vgs(th)) and V24 ≈ 8.6-14.2V (Q_DRIVER turn-on, varies with
Vgs(th) tolerance) where R_GATE_PULL could charge Q1 gate. At
V24 < 8.6V, heater power is < 4.5W per probe (vs 14.4W nominal).
Starting from cold wood at sunrise, this is not a fire risk.
In practice, the buck starts at V24 ≈ 3.5V and the MCU boots within
~5ms, at which point firmware holds PA8 LOW (heater off).

**MCU crash behavior (SCR latch kill path):** If firmware locks up
with PA8 HIGH (heater stuck on), the TPL5010 watchdog fires within
9.6 seconds. The kill sequence:

1. TPL5010 asserts RST (active low) on MCU NRST pin
2. D_ISO (1N4148WS) blocks RST from reaching the SCR latch directly
   (latch only triggers through the watchdog path, not MCU resets)
3. Q_LATCH (MMBT3904 NPN + SS8550 PNP cross-coupled) latches ON
4. Q_WD (2N7002, driven by latch output) pulls Q1 gate to GND
   **permanently** — heater OFF until power cycle
5. Latch overrides R_GATE_PULL (1M): Q_WD sinks only 24 µA,
   pulling gate to ~0.1 mV
6. MCU still boots and can report the fault via RS-485 (D_ISO
   isolates latch from NRST so MCU reset works normally)

**Buck-dead behavior (the scenario that motivated this redesign):**
If 24V is present but 3.3V is dead, the 24V divider holds Q_DRIVER
gate at 4.2V → Q_DRIVER ON → Q1 gate at ~0V → heater OFF. No MCU,
watchdog, or latch needed. The heater is OFF by physics alone.

**Recovery:** Power cycle only. The SCR latch is self-sustaining
once triggered — R_FB (100k) provides base current to maintain the
cross-coupled state. R_LATCH_PD (1M) bleeds the latch when VDD
is removed. This is intentional: a latched heater fault should
require human intervention, not auto-recover.

**State table:**

| State | Q_CTRL | Q_DRIVER | Heater | Safe? |
|-------|--------|----------|--------|-------|
| Sleep (PA8 LOW) | OFF | ON | OFF | Yes |
| Heater pulse (PA8 HIGH) | ON | OFF | ON | Controlled |
| Boot (PA8 float) | OFF | ON | OFF | Yes |
| Buck dead, 24V present | OFF | ON | OFF | Yes |
| MCU crash, PA8 HIGH | ON | OFF | ON | SCR latch 9.6s |
| MCU crash, PA8 LOW | OFF | ON | OFF | Yes |

**Interaction analysis:** The Q_CTRL topology does not affect any
other circuit path. SCR latch (Q_WD on Q1 gate) works unchanged —
Q_WD sinks 24µA from R_GATE_PULL at Rds ~5Ω. PGOOD-gated latch
arming is on a separate node. Sleep current: +4.2µA from 24V
(divider) vs current design. Firmware polarity matches v1.0 (PA8
HIGH = heater ON), simplifying the firmware port.

**Parts:**
- Q_DRIVER: 2N7002 (C8545, already in BOM) -- N-channel, SOT-23
- Q_CTRL: 2N7002 (C8545, already in BOM) -- MCU isolation
- D_ZENER: MM3Z10 (C19077459, preferred, $0.012) -- 10V, SOD-323
- R_GATE_PULL: 1M (C22935, already in BOM)
- R_BIAS: 4.7M (C23163, preferred, $0.0014) -- 24V divider
- R_GATE_PD: 1M (C22935, already in BOM)
- R_CTRL: 10k (C25804, already in BOM) -- PA8 to Q_CTRL gate
- R_CTRL_PD: 100k (C25803, already in BOM) -- boot-safe pull-down

Net new unique parts: 1 (zener diode). All resistors are existing
values. v1.0's R_GATE (1k) and R4 (10k gate pulldown) are removed —
Q_DRIVER replaces both functions.

### MOSFET upgrade

**Current (v1.0):** XCHS3N12 (C48928121), 120V/3A, SOT-23, $0.03
**New:** TM15N10D (C7422818), 100V/15A, DPAK (TO-252-3L), $0.087

| Parameter | v1.0 (3.3V gate) | v1.1 (10V gate via driver) |
|-----------|------------------|---------------------------|
| Vgs(th) | 0.5-1.5V | 1.0-2.0V |
| Rds(on) | ~267 mohm @ 3.3V (est.) | 75 mohm @ 10V (spec) |
| Pdiss @ 1 heater | 87 mW | 24 mW |
| Pdiss @ 2 heaters | 350 mW | 98 mW |
| Pdiss @ 4 heaters | 1.4 W | 391 mW |
| Pdiss @ 8 heaters | 5.6 W (unsafe) | 1,565 mW |
| Package | SOT-23 | DPAK (TO-252-3L) |

**Thermal at 8 heaters:** 1.57W × 20°C/W (DPAK Rth,j-a) = 31°C rise.
At 40°C ambient: Tj = 71°C. At 50°C: Tj = 81°C. Max Tj = 175°C —
comfortable margin. Not trivial dissipation (1.57W), but well within
DPAK capability for 2-second pulses every 30 minutes.

**Layout requirement (DPAK thermal management):** The DPAK exposed
drain tab is the sole heat dissipation path — there is no heatsink,
only PCB copper. Place 4-6 thermal vias (0.3mm drill) under the
drain pad, stitched to a bottom-layer copper pour. At 8 heaters
(1.57W for 2s pulses), transient Rth is ~30% of steady-state: Tj
rise ~9°C per pulse. Without adequate copper/vias, steady-state Rth
can exceed 40°C/W and Tj will approach limits in hot enclosures.

### D1 (reverse polarity Schottky) — moved to buck-only branch

**v1.0 problem:** D1 sits in the series power path before the
buck/heater split, carrying ALL current including heater (up to
4.57A for 8 probes). The SS36 (3A) is undersized, and even an SS56
(5A) has tight thermal margins at 8 heaters in hot enclosures.

**v1.1 fix:** Move D1 after the V24_RAW split point so it protects
only the buck branch (<50 mA). The heater path has no Schottky —
the fuse is the protection element. D1 can remain an SS36 (or any
small SMA Schottky) since it carries milliamps, not amps. Thermal
concern is completely eliminated.

**Reverse polarity behavior (D1 on buck-only):**
- Normal case: TVS forward-clamps V24_RAW to -0.7V. Heater path
  sees -0.7V / 40Ω = 17.5 mA. Harmless. Fuse does NOT blow.
  MOSFET body diode barely conducts. Buck: D1 blocks. Safe.
- TVS failed + reverse polarity: MOSFET body diode conducts,
  fuse blows in ~100ms. Electronics still protected by D1.
  Replace fuse + TVS.
- The M8 upstream connector is keyed — reverse polarity requires
  a wiring error at installation, not a field failure mode.

D1 stays SS36 (C16015, basic, $0.04). No part change needed.

### PTC fuse split topology

**Problem:** v1.0 PTC (1.1A hold) is in the series path before both the
buck converter and heater. At 2+ heaters (1.14A), the PTC trips.

**v1.1 topology:**
```
                    ┌→ D1 (SS36) → PTC (1.1A) → buck input (20 mA steady)
J1 → TVS → V24_RAW ─┤
                    └→ [6A fuse] → heater MOSFET (4.57A pulsed)
```

- D1 moves from the main series path to the buck-only branch. It now
  protects only the electronics (<50 mA). No thermal concern.
- PTC moves from the main series input path (v1.0: before TVS/Schottky)
  to the buck-only branch (v1.1: after D1). It now protects only the
  electronics path (20 mA steady), not the heater.
- Heater path gets a **dedicated fuse** (6A fast-blow, 5x20mm).
  Populated by default — not optional. The fuse is the last line of
  defense for catastrophic shorts (e.g., cable insulation failure in
  the field). User-supplied: any 5-6A fast-blow 5x20mm glass fuse.
- The 4-layer watchdog/latch system handles normal fault modes. The
  fuse handles wiring faults that bypass the electronics entirely.
- TVS sees full current during transients only (microamp leakage in
  steady state). No high-current Schottky in the heater path.

### Multi-heater table

| Heaters | Total current | MOSFET Pdiss (75mΩ @ 10V) | Status |
|---------|--------------|---------------------------|--------|
| 1 | 0.57 A | 24 mW | Easy |
| 2 | 1.14 A | 98 mW | Easy |
| 4 | 2.29 A | 391 mW | OK (Tj rise ~8°C) |
| 8 | 4.57 A | 1,565 mW | OK (Tj rise ~31°C) |

D1 is no longer in the heater path (buck-only branch). No Schottky
thermal concern at any heater count.

### Cable specification

**Topology:** Star. Each heater probe has its own cable pair from the
board to the probe. In star topology, each cable carries only one
probe's current (~0.57A), regardless of total probe count. This makes
cable loss independent of the number of probes.

**Recommended gauge:** 16 AWG (1.31 mm^2) or heavier for cable runs
over 10 meters. At 25m with 16AWG: 3.1% power drop per probe. Maximum
cable length for 20% power drop: **188 meters** (16 AWG star).

| Cable gauge | 25m power drop | Max length (20% drop) |
|-------------|---------------|-----------------------|
| 22 AWG | 11.5% | 47 m |
| 18 AWG | 5.8% | 94 m |
| 16 AWG | 3.1% | 188 m |

**Why power drop matters:** Sap flux methods (Granier, heat ratio) are
ratio-based and self-calibrate per probe — each probe's dTmax is its
own reference. Different cable lengths (and thus different heater powers)
across probes do NOT cause systematic measurement errors. However,
the probe must deliver enough heat to produce a measurable temperature
signal in the wood. At >20% power drop, the temperature rise may be
too small for reliable derivative estimation in highly sap-active trees.

**Shared trunk (NOT recommended for >2 probes):** If all probes share
a single cable pair from the board to a junction box, the trunk carries
the sum of all probe currents. At 8 probes on 22 AWG, 25m trunk: 57%
power drop (insufficient). Even 16 AWG shared trunk at 8 probes: 21%
drop at 25m. Star topology eliminates this scaling problem entirely.

### Heater wiring at the board connector

The 2-pin KF2EDGV-3.5 screw terminal is rated for 10A but physically
accommodates only one wire pair per contact. Deployments with >2 heater
probes MUST use an external junction box or bus bar to fan out star
cables from a single pair of leads into the board connector. This is
standard practice for multi-sensor field instruments (e.g., Campbell
multiplexers use external terminal strips). The junction box should be
inside the weatherproof enclosure, as close to the board as practical.

---

## 5. Input Protection (All Channels)

**Goal:** Identical ESD/EMI protection on all 49 connector-facing analog
lines (48 thermistors + 1 excitation).

Each line gets three protection stages:

1. **TVS array (PRTR5V0U4D):** ESD clamp at connector side. Each IC
   protects 4 lines. 49 lines / 4 = 13 arrays (3 spare channels).
   - v1.0: 2 arrays. v1.1: 13 arrays. Add 11x PRTR5V0U4D (C2835429, $0.09 each).

2. **1k ohm series resistor:** Current limiter + RC filter partner.
   Limits fault current to 3.3 mA. 49 resistors total.
   - v1.0: 7 resistors. v1.1: 49. Add 42x 1k ohm 0603 (C21190, $0.001 each).

3. **100 nF filter cap:** Low-pass filter (fc = 1.6 kHz with 1k ohm).
   Blocks EMI from cables. 49 caps total.
   - v1.0: 7 caps. v1.1: 49. Add 42x 100 nF 0603 (C14663, $0.003 each).

**Zero measurement impact:** The 1k ohm series resistance appears on
BOTH thermistor sense lines AND the excitation sense line (AIN1). In
the ratiometric calculation (V_therm / V_exc), identical voltage
dividers formed by 1k + ADS1115 input impedance (>1 GOhm) cancel.
Mux Ron (~80 ohm) appears only in the thermistor path, but with >1 GOhm
load, the voltage drop is negligible (16 uV from input leakage).

**Unused mux channels:** Tie to GND. Prevents floating CMOS inputs
from coupling noise.

**Cost for additional channels:** +$1.14 (11 TVS + 42 R + 42 C)

### ESD rail isolation (ferrite bead)

With 13 PRTR5V0U4D arrays, ESD events on any connector pin dump transient
current into the TVS VCC rail. Without isolation, this current flows
directly into the 3.3V bus shared with the MCU, ADCs, and EEPROM —
potentially corrupting an in-progress ADC conversion or causing a
brownout reset.

**Fix:** Add a ferrite bead (L3) between the main 3.3V rail and the
TVS VCC bus, splitting the supply into "clean 3.3V" (MCU, ADCs, EEPROM,
flash) and "dirty 3.3V" (TVS array VCC pins only). ESD energy stays
local to the TVS side; the ferrite's high impedance at MHz frequencies
blocks the transient from reaching sensitive analog circuitry.

```
V3V3 (clean) ──── L3 (ferrite) ──── V3V3_TVS (dirty)
  │                                      │
  ├── MCU                                ├── 13x PRTR5V0U4D VCC
  ├── 2x ADS1115                         └── 100nF local decoupling
  ├── EEPROM
  ├── Flash
  └── SP3485
```

**Part:** GZ1608D601TF (C1002), 600 ohm @ 100 MHz, 0603, basic, $0.008.
Same part as L2 (VDDA ferrite) — no new BOM line item. Add one 100 nF
decoupling cap (C14663) on the TVS side.

**DC impact:** At DC the ferrite is ~0.2 ohm. TVS arrays draw <1 uA
quiescent. Voltage drop: negligible. During an ESD event the ferrite
presents >600 ohm to the transient, attenuating it by >50 dB before
it reaches the clean rail.

---

### Power pin changes

- VBAT (pin 1): disconnected from VDDA_FILT, routed through BAT54S
  from VDD and CR2032

### Freed pins

- PB1: was ADC2 ALERT/DRDY (2nd ADS1115 removed)

### Spare GPIOs (12 total)

PA6, PA7, PA15, PB1, PB2, PB8, PB9, PB10, PB11, PC13, PF0, PF1

PA6 and PA7 are broken out on the auxiliary header for external use.

**LQFP-48 port availability (verified):** PA0-PA15, PB0-PB15,
PC6, PC7, PC13, PC14, PC15, PD0-PD3, PF0, PF1. No other PC or PD
pins exist on this package (PC0-PC5, PC8-PC12, PD4+ are only on
LQFP-64/100).

**SPI1 conflict note:** SPI1_SCK maps to PA5, which is already used by
TPL5010 DONE. SPI2 on PB12-PB15 avoids this conflict entirely.

**I2C note:** Run at 100 kHz (standard mode). With single ADS1115's
10k pull-ups, rise time is 424 ns at 50 pF bus -- fine for standard
mode (spec: < 1000 ns) but marginal for 400 kHz fast mode (spec:
< 300 ns). No hardware change needed. If external I2C sensors are
connected via the 48-pin header (pins 43-44) on long cables, the
added bus capacitance may require stronger pull-ups (4.7k or 2.2k).
Evaluate after first field deployment.
